# Introduction

We describe BMI–hypercapnia relationships within a selected acute-care cohort while exposing how historical source-entry pathways shape the observed population. These pathways record representation in reason-for-suspicion (RFS) source files; they do not necessarily identify every clinical criterion present at an encounter. Separating entry routes can change the observed association itself and does not eliminate outcome-dependent selection.

# Methods

## Source, eligibility and fixed index

The authenticated original FULL_DATA encounter list defines candidate visits. Adults had a 2022 emergency or inpatient encounter and available valid BMI ≥30 kg/m². Age uses the inherited birth-year proxy. Each patient contributes the first qualifying encounter before gas availability and adjustment completeness. Earlier unresolved eligibility, conflicting evidence and earliest-date ties remain unresolved. Later encounters never replace an obesity-only index.

BMI follows the approved encounter/prior reported-value hierarchy, followed by calculation from observed height and weight, with inherited rounding and validity rules. One-unit diagnostic bins around BMI 40 and 50 describe measurement and selection; they are not a regression-discontinuity design. No statistical BMI imputation is performed. Available BMI is not necessarily contemporaneous with the outcome. The audit reports measurement methods, lags, unknown chronology and consequences of the existing rules. Signed lags equal encounter-start date minus measurement date: positive means prior, zero means the same calendar day, and negative means later during the encounter. Component gaps are absolute differences between height and weight dates.

## Historical source-entry populations

A confirmed positive ABG, VBG, RESPFAIL, VENTSUPPORT or PREDISPOSITION source flag establishes the primary population, including encounters also represented through OBESITY. Obesity-only membership requires OBESITY and authenticated zeros in all five other families. Obesity-only indexes are excluded from scientific comparisons: removing the gas-related entry pathways selects against the evidence needed to assess the physiological outcomes. Their counts remain in the flow for reconciliation; source discrepancies and descriptive profiles are confined to the audit. Unknown flags remain unknown. All-six-zero discrepancies require source investigation. RFS metadata are applied after the common index is selected.

The combined indexed cohort is a reconciliation reference. Non-OBESITY-only, overlapping and unknown-OBESITY/confirmed-non-OBESITY subgroups are descriptive. BMI ≥40 remains a descriptive stratum and is not equated with obesity-route membership. An overlapping all-OBESITY supporting analysis is confined to the audit.

## Outcomes and adjustment

Arterial hypercapnia requires ordinary authenticated ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 mm Hg. Combined gas accepts ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 or VBG PvCO~2~ ≥50 mm Hg; both specimens are not required. No pH restriction is applied to the established primary outcomes. Strict validity limits are 5<arterial<200 and 10<venous<250 mm Hg, with reviewed units. Available-evidence negatives do not establish that an unmeasured specimen is normal. Unusable or unavailable outcomes remain unknown.

The ICD composite comprises J96.02, J96.12, J96.22, J96.92 and E66.2, with captured absence negative only under complete diagnosis capture. E66.2 introduces obesity-related ascertainment. Index-calendar-day gas sensitivities use recorded-result date equal to encounter-start date, retaining the index. This export does not authenticate collection times.

Adjustment retains linear age and the inherited sex, combined race/ethnicity and geographic-region coding. Completeness means nonmissing values for inherited analysis variables, including retained Unknown categories. The White reference category includes non-Hispanic or unknown ethnicity; inherited race-category precedence is unchanged. Raw race × ethnicity cross-tabs are shown only when authenticated.

## Models, probabilities and uncertainty

Primary models use type-7 BMI quantiles .05/.35/.65/.95 from the primary adjustment-complete population: two interior knots, two boundaries and three natural-spline basis columns. The basis remains fixed across primary outcomes, timing, matched analyses and predictions. The primary current-measurement sensitivity reuses this basis. The overlapping all-OBESITY supporting analysis uses its own basis and is reported in the audit. Obesity-only and obesity-only current-measurement models are not registered. Constant outcomes, duplicate knots, separation, rank and convergence failures in planned models remain explicit without estimator substitution.

Gas curves standardize over each model's outcome-evaluable population; ICD uses known capture within group. Observation curves describe usable gas-evidence availability. Complete diagnosis capture is reported as a source fact, not as ICD positivity or a constant availability curve. No physiological outcomes are projected to untested patients. Fixed BMI 45 versus 40 contrasts require training-range support. Local counts and marginal covariate coverage expose sparsity even inside the global BMI range; these checks do not establish joint covariate support.

Pointwise 95% intervals use full coefficient covariance and condition on the empirical reference and fixed spline basis. They omit uncertainty from selection, measurement error and unmeasured confounding. Apparent calibration is in-sample; fitted/observed mean agreement is not independent validation.

## Secondary scenario and supporting checks

The named secondary scenario subtracts exactly one BMI unit when observed BMI >30; BMI=30 is unchanged. There is no floor or reselection. Paired predictions hold index, RFS membership and other covariates fixed. Reported quantities are observed and shifted mean probabilities, their signed difference and PIF=1−p_shifted/p_observed. Signed original-BMI-band contributions and their full covariance reproduce the total difference and variance. Marginal curve-density integration is not used.

Same-sample linear-BMI checks and matched ICD/gas analyses remain registered. A limited current-measurement sensitivity uses the already-selected BMI when reported at the index or calculated from height and weight both authenticated to that encounter. Full-cohort MAR/MNAR projections and IPW are excluded. The report is rendered from saved aggregates without clinical reads or refitting.

## Same-day arterial PCO₂/pH co-occurrence

This secondary analysis uses any recorded calendar date within the existing index encounter with both usable ordinary arterial PCO~2~ and arterial pH. It is **same recorded-day co-occurrence; not verified same-sample pairing**. The export dates when results were recorded; it does not identify a shared blood sample, collection time or elapsed 24-hour interval. Validity screens are 5<PCO~2~<200 mm Hg and 6.5<pH<7.8, applied before display rounding.

The source endpoints use the same patients with at least one co-observed day: any PaCO~2~ ≥45 on such a day, and any such day also containing pH <7.35. Results may come from different samples. Elevated PCO~2~ on one date and low pH on another cannot establish co-occurrence. Patients without a valid co-observed day have unknown supplemental outcomes. Additional unusable or single-analyte records remain audited without erasing usable days. A negative describes eligible recorded evidence only. The primary numeric BMI spline basis, inherited adjustment and common supplemental reference population are retained. A single unpenalized multinomial logistic spline assigns each patient to no documented hypercapnia, hypercapnia without documented same-day acidemia, or hypercapnia with same-day acidemia. Any eligible hypercapnia–acidemia day takes priority, including patients with other hypercapnic days without acidemia. The baseline outcome is no documented hypercapnia. All three probabilities are standardized over the same patients; full cross-category covariance supplies pointwise intervals and comparisons of component changes. No additional PIF is calculated.

The full observed BMI range is the main relationship, with sparse regions flagged. BMI 40–45 is a prespecified numerical summary, not a biological cutoff or fitting restriction. Every supported five-unit interval is also reported. These are descriptive pointwise contrasts without multiplicity adjustment; separate significance counts do not establish differences in associations.

```{r}
#| label: same-day-abg-supplement
#| results: asis
bmi_report_table(a$cooccurrence_status,"Recorded-day source qualification",keys="module")
z<-a$cooccurrence_reconciliation
shown<-data.frame(Stage=z$stage,Patients=z$n,Events=z$events,
  Observed=ifelse(is.na(z$proportion),"Unavailable",sprintf("%.2f%% (95%% CI %.2f–%.2f%%)",100*z$proportion,100*z$conf_low,100*z$conf_high)),Status=z$status)
bmi_report_table(shown,"Four-stage patient/evidence reconciliation; raw proportions with Wilson 95% intervals",keys="Stage")
figure("S1-same-day-ABG")
bmi_report_table(a$cooccurrence_categories,"Mutually exclusive patient categories; any acidemia co-occurrence takes priority",keys="category_id")
bmi_report_table(bmi_same_day_contrast_view(a$same_day_contrasts),"Component magnitudes across BMI: absolute changes in percentage points and probability ratios, with 95% intervals",keys=c("BMI interval","Outcome"))
bmi_report_table(a$same_day_curve_reconciliation,"Joint probability and stacked-component reconciliation",keys="status")
```

Requiring both analytes on the same date introduces additional selection. The reconciliation separates patient restriction, restriction to co-observed days, and addition of low pH. Values can represent different samples or periods before and after treatment; co-occurrence does not establish simultaneous hypercapnic acidemia, acute respiratory failure or chronic compensation. Primary arterial findings on other dates remain unchanged. The joint model guarantees coherent category probabilities without clipping. In the stacked panel, band thickness is the component probability and the upper boundary is total hypercapnia. The common-baseline panel shows both components with their own intervals. The signed with-minus-without change contrasts use joint covariance; interval overlap is not the comparison test. Neither documented category establishes chronic compensation or the mechanism of acidemia.

## Documented respiratory-failure acuity and OHS

This supplement partitions the inherited five-code ICD composite on the same fixed primary indexes. It requires complete encounter diagnosis capture and nonmissing inherited adjustment variables, including retained Unknown categories; it does not require blood gas evidence. J96.22 or J96.02 together with J96.12/E66.2 receives priority as **acute-on-chronic or concurrent acute/chronic coding**. Remaining J96.02 is acute; remaining J96.12/E66.2 is chronic coding/OHS; remaining J96.92 is unspecified acuity. No target code with complete capture is the reference category. Incomplete capture is unknown. OHS is grouped analytically with chronic coding and does not itself establish chronic respiratory failure.

One Firth mean-bias-reduced five-category multinomial spline reuses the primary numeric BMI basis, linear age and inherited sex, race/ethnicity and region adjustment. All class probabilities are standardized over the same diagnosis-evaluable patients. The estimator maximizes the multinomial log likelihood plus one half of the log determinant of its Fisher information. It replaces a separated unpenalized fit without pooling demographic levels or changing categories. The inverse multinomial information at the bias-reduced estimate supplies first-order joint covariance, with the empirical reference and numeric spline held fixed. This finite-estimate method does not resolve sparse support, source selection or measurement bias. Full joint covariance supplies pointwise 95% intervals, supported five-unit changes and pairwise differences in those changes. These descriptive comparisons are not multiplicity adjusted. The fitted positive components sum to the joint composite; it need not equal the existing binary model's predictions. Primary estimates, S1 and PIFs remain unchanged; no supplemental PIF is calculated.

```{r}
#| label: icd-acuity-supplement
#| results: asis
bmi_report_table(a$icd_acuity_status,"ICD code-level source qualification",keys="module")
fit<-a$model_registry[a$model_registry$family %in% c("icd_acuity","icd_acuity_specified"),]
bmi_report_table(fit[c("model_id","estimator","n_model","status","failure_reason")],"ICD model estimability; source qualification does not imply a successful fit",keys="model_id")
if(any(!fit$status %in% c("successful","fitted_with_concerns")))cat("\n\nOne or more planned ICD positions is nonestimable; its explicit status is retained. No additional fallback was substituted.\n\n")
z<-a$icd_acuity_categories
shown<-data.frame(Category=z$label,Patients=z$n,N=z$N,
  Observed=ifelse(is.na(z$proportion),"Unavailable",sprintf("%.2f%% (95%% CI %.2f–%.2f%%)",100*z$proportion,100*z$conf_low,100*z$conf_high)),Status=z$status)
bmi_report_table(shown,"Mutually exclusive ICD categories; observed proportions with Wilson 95% intervals",keys="Category")
figure("S2-ICD-acuity")
labels<-c(bmi_icd_labels,any_target="Any target diagnosis")
spec<-bmi_icd_spec()
for(i in seq_along(spec$contrast_pairs)) {
 pair<-spec$contrast_pairs[[i]]
 labels[spec$contrast_names[i]]<-paste(bmi_icd_labels[pair[1]],"minus",bmi_icd_labels[pair[2]],": difference in changes")
}
for(id in fit$model_id) {
 cat("\n\n### ",if(grepl("icd_acuity_specified/",id))"Four-category sensitivity"else"Five-category bias-reduced model","\n\n",sep="")
 z<-a$icd_acuity_contrasts[a$icd_acuity_contrasts$model_id==id,]
 bmi_report_table(bmi_same_day_contrast_view(z,labels),"ICD component magnitudes and differences in BMI-associated changes; 95% intervals",keys=c("BMI interval","Outcome"))
}
cat("\n\nThe unpenalized four-category sensitivity excludes only the final unspecified-only category. Mixed codes assigned to specified categories remain included. It retains the primary basis and adjustment but uses its own reduced fitting and standardization population; this is not a same-denominator estimator comparison. Persistent separation is an explicit failure, not an invitation to substitute an estimator.\n\n")
figure("S2-ICD-specified")
figure("S2-ICD-observed")
bmi_report_table(a$icd_acuity_reconciliation,"Original composite and subtype reconciliation",keys="metric")
```

Diagnostic codes reflect documentation and historical source-entry selection. Acute coding is not acidemia, and chronic coding is not evidence of physiological compensation. OHS includes obesity in its definition; a BMI association in that component may partly reflect diagnostic incorporation. The audit retains the five-code patterns, explicit versus concurrent coding, and OHS versus chronic respiratory-failure composition by BMI and source-entry subgroup. This supplement does not establish incident disease or causal effects.

# Discussion and example conclusion

The primary analysis estimates BMI relationships among non-OBESITY-supported indexes while preserving the same clinical episode. Excluding an obesity-only entry route does not remove outcome-dependent entry or selective gas measurement from the retained population. No weighting or transport to excluded indexes is attempted: near-absent gas observation in the excluded entry route does not supply an independent physiological comparator. The overlapping supporting analyses remain in the audit and do not constitute between-group tests.

A defensible conclusion should describe the direction and shape actually supported by the primary curves and the outcome-dependent selection exposed by the evidence audit. No claim of preventable disease or treatment benefit follows from the secondary scenario. Selection into the original files, selective gas measurement, BMI timing and measurement uncertainty, residual confounding and sparse tails remain limitations.

The accompanying audit retains full model output, reconciliation and supporting analyses. Source acceptance, numerical review, visual inspection and investigator scientific approval are distinct states.
